title: Seeing Is Not Acting: WARD Diagnoses the Evidence-to-State-to-Action Gap in Longitudinal Clinical Agents
why_read: A rigorous benchmark exposing a specific failure mode in clinical LLM agents, namely that they recognize new evidence but fail to act on it, which is clinically important.
analysis: WARD is a benchmark testing whether AI clinical agents correctly update patient-state judgments and actions as new evidence arrives over a hospital stay, rather than just answering isolated questions. It uses thousands of tasks derived from real longitudinal hospitalization trajectories, with separate tracks for passive evidence tracking and interactive tool-based management. The key finding is stark: models recognize relevant evidence most of the time but fail to translate it into correct state updates or actions in the vast majority of cases, and only about 11% of agent actions in the interactive track actually advanced patient care appropriately. This is valuable for anyone building or evaluating medical AI agents, since it highlights a concrete gap between perception and safe action that simpler benchmarks miss.
